content: HCN1, also known as potassium/sodium hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated channel 1, is a protein encoded by the HCN1 gene in humans. The hyperpolarization-activated cation channels belonging to the HCN gene family, including HCN1, play a critical role in generating spontaneous rhythmic activity in both the heart and the brain. The HCN1 channel is expressed in several specific tissues, including the sinoatrial node of the heart, the neocortex, the hippocampus, the cerebellar cortex, the dorsal root ganglion, the trigeminal ganglion, and the brainstem. HCN1 has been demonstrated to interact with another member of the HCN family, HCN2. De novo mutations in the HCN1 gene have been identified as a cause of epilepsy.
